correctness.rationale: For nonempty binary non-overlapping codes, length-one prefix/suffix restrictions force a common first bit and opposite last bit; complementation normalizes to 0...1. All self-unbordered normalized words of length 2..n form vertices of the compatibility graph, with incompatibility exactly cross-prefix/suffix overlaps or substring containment. Cliques are exactly admissible codes. The package ordered bitset recursion uses independent color classes as legitimate clique upper bounds and shortest remaining lengths as legitimate total-length lower bounds, with no incomplete stopping rule. An INDEPENDENT sparse 0/1 MILP reconstructed all conflict pairs and proved optimality with solver optimal status and zero MIP gap at all nine n=2..10: (m_n,T_n)=(1,2),(1,2),(1,2),(2,9),(3,16),(5,32),(8,59),(14,119),(24,227); candidate count at n=10 is 295. Thus the finite exact result, with explicit 13 length-9 and 11 length-10 witness words at n=10, is correct. The MILP exact optimum is finite and does not prove results n>10.
residual_risks: Finite result only through n=10; no unbounded capacity formula or all-optima classification.
MILP optimality is a computational finite certificate with independently reconstructed feasible graph, not a formal infinite theorem.

The n=10 optimum of 227 saves 13 bits relative to uniform-length 24-codeword realizations and identifies a reproducible boundary for future improved constructions.
